Summary: Java source attachment lost when same JAR added to another project (1GDKX8O)
Description: The Java source attachment for an external JAR gets lost when the same JAR is \\nadded to another project. While it is a desirable feature that all source attachments\\nare maintained at the workspace level (i.e., shared between probjects), this bug \\ncripples that feature.\\n\\n1. create a Java project P1; add an external JAR to P1\\n	D:/eclipse105-jdk/eclipse/plugins/org.eclipse.core.runtime/runtime.zip\\nwith source attachment\\n	D:/eclipse105-jdk/eclipse/plugins/org.eclipse.core.runtime/runtimesrc.zip\\n\\n2. In package view of P1, select the JAR and open its Properties.\\n\\nObserve: It has a Java source attachment.\\n\\n3. create a Java project P2; add the same external JAR to P2\\n	D:/eclipse105-jdk/eclipse/plugins/org.eclipse.core.runtime/runtime.zip\\nwith no source attachment\\n\\n4. In package view of P1, select the JAR and open its Properties.\\n\\nObserve: It has lost its Java source attachment.\\n\\nExpectation: As soon as I said I wanted to add the JAR, it should have\\nrecognized that this JAR was already known in this workspace to have\\na source attachment. The source attachment should have been picked\\nup and preserved (and had I opened the subdialog to set the source\\nattachment, I should see the value already primed).\\n\\nNOTES:\\n\\nOT (17/05/2001 3:53:28 PM)\\n	The problem seems to be related to the fact that the source attachement property are stored according to the path. So for two external jars the source attachement property is\\n	identical. Then when adding the second time the same external jar to a different project, the source attachement of the first one is deleted.\\n	The following method should test if the root has a source attachement path before deleting it. In the example, entry.getSourceAttachementPath() and \\n	entry.getSourceAttachmentRootPath() are null when we add the second external jar without any source attachement. But if you check the value of root.getSourceAttachementPath()\\n	and root.getSourceAttachmentRootPath() before executing root.attachSource(sourcePath, sourcePrefix, null); you will find that the two values are not null and point to the previous\\n	source attachement settings for the first external jar added in the first project.\\n\\norg.eclipse.jdt.internal.ui.wizards.buildpaths.BuildPathsBlock.attachSource(IPath, CPListElement)\\n	private void attachSource(IPath path, CPListElement entry) throws CoreException {\\n		IPackageFragmentRoot root= fCurrJProject.findPackageFragmentRoot(path);\\n		if (root != null && root.isArchive()) {\\n			IPath sourcePath= entry.getSourceAttachmentPath();\\n			IPath sourcePrefix= entry.getSourceAttachmentRootPath();\\n			root.attachSource(sourcePath, sourcePrefix, null);\\n			JavaDocAccess.setJavaDocLocation(root, entry.getJavaDocLocation());\\n		}\\n	}\\n\\n	Should move to ITPJUI.\\n\\nMA (5/22/01 4:38:14 PM)\\n	lots of changes with source attachments\\n	please verify\\n\\nPA (5/29/01 2:44:18 PM)\\n	build 113\\n	still problems:\\n	- 2 Projects\\n	- both use the same rt.jar and src.jar (but dont take ./jre/rt.jar, use rt.jar and src.jar provided by JDK)\\n	-> 2nd project has no source attachment !\\n\\nMA (5/30/01 6:15:13 PM)\\n	cant reproduce. asked P for a reproducable case

Summary: classpath lost when creating a Java project with existing .classpath file (1GDKFWO)
Description: I have a directory containing a Java project created on an earlier\\noccasion (in a different workspace). I want to create a new workspace\\nand re-create that project and use the existing directory. I can't\\nseem to do this without losing the class information.\\n\\nSteps to reproduce:\\n\\n1. Launch eclipse; create a Java project named \\"Hello Project\\" with\\nsource files from /Hello Project/src; create /Hello Project/src/HelloWorld.java\\n(i.e., in the default package); build; exit eclipse.\\n\\n2. Launch eclipse for a new workspace (I did this using a separate\\ninstall of eclipse).\\n\\n3. Create a new Java project specifying the location of the existing\\n\\"Hello Project\\" project directory inside the old workspace.\\n\\nObserve: Although there are local files existing on disk at the project\\nlocation, they are not accessed immediately. In particular, the classpath\\nin the dialog comes up empty. If I proceed, the existing .classpath file\\nis overwritten and the previously-set classpath is lost.\\n\\nExpectation: When a project is being created in the workbench, there is\\nalways the possibility that the files for the project already exist on disk.\\nIf they do exist, they should be used; if they do not, they should be created.\\n\\nNOTES:\\n\\nPM (5/14/2001 11:24:42 AM)\\n	I think the problem comes from the fact you use the UI wizard which does enforce a classpath initialization.\\n	This takes precedence over an eventual .classpath file existency (which is only read when opening the Java project), in fact it\\n	will be rewritten before the Java model can read it. Unclear though if existing APIs allow to solve this one, but this sounds like\\n	a problem which could affect WSA as well.\\n\\n	Moving to Java UI.\\n	\\nEG (5/28/01 4:38:46 PM)\\n	The Wizard could check whether a .classpath exists before initializing a new one.\\n	This might require additional API to refresh the project's build path from the .classpath file. \\n\\nMA (20.08.2001 17:46:23)\\n	I think, the New Java Project wizard should be allowed to assume that the project is not existing.\\n\\n	I guess I would have to set the Java nature first, no have access to the existing .classpath file.\\n	This, however, I can not do before the user pressed finished (cancel is always possible).\\n\\n	The feature sounds more like a 'Add existing project' where you can specify the location of an existing project, and\\n	mount it in your workspace. I think this could be supported by the desktop in general (not only for Java project).\\n	What is needed is the information of the '.vcm_meta' file.\\n	\\n	Why isn't '.classpath' part of '.vcm_meta'?\\n	We should have one project description file, containing all project specific settings.

Summary: Project dependencies not updated when .classpath file is read-only[PR 1GLEVO4]
Description: PR 1GLEVO4\\n\\nCASE 1: \\n1) Create two Java projects  Project1  and Project2\\n2) Make the .classpath file for  Project1 read-only  (RMB on .classpath file, \\nchoose Properties, check read only)\\n3) Update Project1's Java Build Path to include Project2  (RMB on Project1, \\nchoose Properties, choose Java Build Path, choose Projects tab)\\n4) To the user it looks like this has occurred without problem (it's still in \\nProject1's Java Build Path, and calls to the JavaModel return the correct \\ninformation)\\nbut since the .classpath file is read-only, this change has never occured).  At \\nthis point we believe the user should have been told that the\\nfile could not be updated.\\n5) Bring down the workbench and bring it back up, and it is no longer in  \\nProject1's Java Build Path.\\n\\n\\nCASE 2: \\nHere is another scenario (which I have not verified, but it seems right): \\n\\nThe programmer creates a new project called ABC and does not chose to use the \\ndefault directory. Instead, he \\npoints to the directory in Clearcase containing the existing project files.\\n\\nAs part of the Java project create, it creates a new .classpath file. It does \\nnot look to see if there is an \\nexisting .classpath file (where in this case there is and its read-only). \\nBecause we are talking about a \\nClearcase controlled directory, the project create process results in a private \\nread-write copy of the .classpath \\nfile being created. For example, if the\\n * declaring type associated with this stack frame is \\"org.eclipse.example.Example\\", \\n * the associated source name would be \\"Example.java\\".\\n * \\n * @return unqualified source file name, or null\\n * @excetpion DebugException if an exception occurrs retrieving the name from the target\\n */\\n public String getSourceName();\\n\\njeem (5/10/01 2:01:58 PM) - Yep. Description: Please split the \\"Use 'src' and 'bin' folders as default in new Java projects\\" \\npreference into two separate preferences as follows:\\n[ ] \\"Use 'src' folder as default in new Java projects\\"\\n[ ] \\"Use 'bin' folder as default in new Java projects\\"\\n\\nThe best way to describe why I would like this is to paste here a posting I \\njust made to Eclipse Corner that describes how I work. Summary: UI to easily create or manage //$NON-NLS-x$ markers
Description: It is often the case that the knowledge that some constant string is non-localisable exists at the time the string is created.  In such cases it is convenient to mark the string with the special //$NON-NLS-x$ comment in order to have it passed over as a candidate for indirection to a resource bundle.  However, there is no easy way to do this, other than typing this comment by hand, copy and pasting it (updating the ordinal) or perhaps using a template which trivially expands to the NON-NLS comment.\\n\\nIt would be nice to have a way to hint at the status of a string during editing.  Perhaps strings could be syntax highlighted (e.g. coloured) in different ways depending on whether NON-NLS comments existed for them, and it would be great if their state could be toggled with a context menu option.\\n\\nAnother aspect of convenience, would be to have the editor keep track of the string ordinals and which strings are marked as not externalisable.  If I insert, remove or reorder strings on the line, it would be great to have the comments update to reflect the new ordinals of the non-externaliable strings.\\n\\nFinally, it is not possible to use templates at present to allow new NON-NLS comments to be quickly added at the end of a line.  This works for the first case, but the template expansion mechanism is sensitive to the cursor being within a line comment, so attempting to add 2nd and subsequent comments to the right of the 1st will not work.

Summary: Allow env variable for Java Source Attachement of jars besides JRE [build path]
Description: I work on projects with other people who don't have the J2SDK/JREs installed in\\nthe same place, i.e. on the same drive and directory. To preclude classpath\\nconflicts (the .classpath file for a project is under CVS) Eclipse thoughtfully\\nuses reserved environmental variables for the Java Source Attachment in the\\nproperties of the JRE_LIB for a given project. However, for other jar files, for\\nexample log4j.jar, there is no \\"Env Var\\" button for the Java Source Attachment\\nin the properties dialog - one is forced to specify a path either in the\\nfilesystem or in the workspace. Putting the jar file in the workspace avoids\\nconflicts, but since the Preferences allows the creation of custom env\\nvariables, why not add the option to use one of them for the Java Source\\nAttachment analog to how it works for the JRE_LIB? Then it would not be\\nnecessary to import all the jar files  into a project just to be able to jump\\ninto the source.

Summary: Allow unzipped source for Java Source Attachment [build path]
Description: There seems to be an inconsistency in how the Java Source Attachment is done for\\nthe JRE versus everything else. In the J2SDK directory (specified as the JRE to\\nuse), it is necessary to unjar the src.jar file (JRE 1.3) or unzip the src.zip\\nfile (JRE 1.4 to a src subdirectory in order for Eclipse to be able to find and\\njump into the source files. However, when specifying the Java Source Attachment\\nfor anything else, only a jar or zip file can be specified - a directory is not\\nallowed. So if a distribution of a 3rd party product is installed (even if\\nmerely unzipped) analgous to how the J2SDK/JRE is installed, and doesn't have a\\nseparately zipped source inside that, but rather a src directory, then one is\\nforced to jar the source files (or alternatively use a copy of the original zip\\nfile).\\n\\nSince in the latter case, Eclipse can jump into source in a jar/zip file, why is\\nit necessary to unpack the src.jar or src.zip in the J2SDK installation?\\n\\nAnd since in the former case, Eclipse can use an unpacked source directory, why\\nis it not allowed to use one for other stuff?\\n\\nHow about making both work with both?

Summary: Organizing imports doesn't pick up the right type
Description: Using 0508, I got invalid imports after doing an \\"organizing imports\\" action. I isolated a simple \\ntest case:\\n\\nFirst class:\\n[package p1;\\n\\npublic class A {\\n\\n	public static void foo() \\n{\\n	}\\n}]\\n\\nSecond class:\\n[package p2;\\n\\npublic class A {\\n	public static void foo() \\n{\\n	}\\n}]\\n\\nThird class:\\n[package p3;\\n\\nimport p1.*;\\n\\npublic class B {\\n\\n	public \\nstatic void bar() {\\n		p2.A.foo();\\n	}\\n	public static void main(String[] args) \\n{\\n		A.foo();\\n	}\\n}]\\n\\nThe \\"Organizing imports\\" action is done on that last class. The \\nresult is:\\n\\n[package p3;\\n\\nimport p2.A;\\n\\npublic class B {\\n\\n	public static void bar() \\n{\\n		p2.A.foo();\\n	}\\n	public static void main(String[] args) \\n{\\n		A.foo();\\n	}\\n}]\\n\\nHaving only p2.A is incorrect, because the line A.foo() was \\nactually referring to p1.A.foo() and not p2.A.foo(). I checked that the DOM/AST binding \\nresolution returns two different bindings for the two names (p2.A or A) and (A in A.foo()). We have \\np1.A and p2.A, but the resulting import contains only p2.A. So I wonder why p1.A has been removed. \\nFuthermore I think that fully qualified name should never be investigated in this case. p2.A is \\nenough and there is no need to have this import in the import's declarations. In this case, having \\np1.A and p2.A would result in a conflict and this is why p2.A has been used as a fully qualified name \\nreference in the source. I think it is crucial that \\"Organize imports\\" handles this case \\nproperly. I found it in the JDTCore sources and this led to a message could not be retrieved. So even \\nif the code compiles fine, the \\"Organizing imports\\" had a side-effect on the runtime. In order to be \\nuseful and safely use, this needs to be fixed. This is why I set the severity to major.

Summary: Caller of Signature.toString(String) should be aware that it won't work for '$' separated top-level types (1G4QB2S)
Description: Signature.toString(String) has been changed to handle '$' in inner types signatures. Summary: Huge number of warnings now generated by JDTCompilerAdapter
Description: Between versions 2.0.1 and 2.0.2, JDTCompilerAdapter has changed the warnings \\nproduced by the compiler from:\\n\\n-warn:constructorName,packageDefaultMethod,maskedCatchBlocks,deprecation\\n\\nto\\n\\n-\\nwarn:constructorName,packageDefaultMethod,maskedCatchBlocks,unusedLocals,unusedA\\nrguments,unusedImports,syntheticAccess,assertIdentifier\\n\\nThe addition of the extra options means that running Ant now generates a huge \\nnumber of warnings on our source tree. The warnings are collected in the Log \\nConsole, which seems to get slower and slower, and our Ant build has become \\nimpossibly slow (it was less than 1 minute and is now over 20 minutes - at \\nwhich point I killed the process).\\n\\nWe can work around the problem by using the Ant \\"nowarn\\" option to disable the \\nwarnings, but we would ideally like to have some of the warnings turned on.\\n\\nI'd be happy if the warnings were changed back to those used by v2.0.1. \\nHowever, perhaps it would be possible to use an Ant property to define the list \\nof warnings? Ant's jikes wrapper does this for extra options (see the bottom of \\nthis page: http://jakarta.apache.org/ant/manual/CoreTasks/javac.html ).

Most commonly, statements are broken directly after \\nthe '=', ';', ')', '.' or ',' characters, after or before \\nthe '||', '&&', '|', '&' or '!' operators, after or before keywords \\nlike 'extends', 'throws', 'implements', etc.\\n\\nI'll use a notation where I show a snippet of code labeled before and a snippet \\nof code labeled after. The before code is roughly what a long statement would \\nlook like. The after code is what the statement should look like after the \\ndeveloper breaks the statement to multiple lines and continuation indentation \\nhas taken place. For most examples, I'll provide one example with the before \\nstatement broken into two lines and second example witht eh before statement \\nbroken into three lines.\\n\\nNormally, continuation indent has multiple settings. And I think\\nI found a bug for JDTCompilerAdapter.\\nSee at :\\nhttp://dev.eclipse.org/viewcvs/index.cgi/org.eclipse.jdt.core/antadapter/org/eclipse/jdt/core/JDTCompilerAdapter.java?rev=1.20&content-type=text/vnd.viewcvs-markup\\n\\nI can see :\\n\\n\\n	/*\\n		 * Handle the nowarn option. If none, then we generate all warnings.\\n		 */		\\n        if (attributes.getNowarn()) {\\n			if (deprecation) {\\n				cmd.createArgument().setValue(\\"-warn:allDeprecation\\"); //$NON-NLS-1$\\n			} else {\\n	            cmd.createArgument().setValue(\\"-nowarn\\"); //$NON-NLS-1$\\n			}\\n        } else {\\n			/*\\n			 * deprecation option.\\n			 */		\\n			if (deprecation) {\\n				cmd.createArgument().setValue(\\n				\\n\\"-warn:allDeprecation,constructorName,packageDefaultMethod,maskedCatchBlocks,unusedImports,staticReceiver\\");\\n//$NON-NLS-1$\\n			} else {\\n				cmd.createArgument().setValue(\\n				\\n\\"-warn:constructorName,packageDefaultMethod,maskedCatchBlocks,unusedImports,staticReceiver\\");\\n//$NON-NLS-1$\\n			}\\n        }\\n\\n\\n\\nAs you can see, when getNoWarn is false, every warning level are\\nwritten INSIDE the code (hard coding).\\nIt doesn't use user's preferences.

Summary: White space options for method and constructor declarations

E.g: \\n\\nFORMATTER_INSERT_SPACE_BEFORE_COMMA_IN_METHOD_ARGUMENTS\\nversus\\nFORMATTER_INSERT_SPACE_BEFORE_COMMA_IN_CONSTRUCTOR_ARGUMENTS\\n\\nBut on the other hand, to control the spaces around the parens/braces,\\nconstructors and methods have common options. E.g.:\\n\\nFORMATTER_INSERT_SPACE_BEFORE_METHOD_DECLARATION_OPEN_PAREN\\n would be splitted into \\nFORMATTER_INSERT_SPACE_BEFORE_METHOD_DECLARATION_OPEN_PAREN\\nand \\nFORMATTER_INSERT_SPACE_BEFORE_CONSTRUCTOR_DECLARATION_OPEN_PAREN\\n\\nThe other possibility would be to merge all settings and not to make a\\ndifference between constructors and methods at all. Summary: Provide batch invocation of code formatter
Description: To help ensure code consistency and standards, it would be very useful if\\nthe source formatter could be invoked in batch. Although a large majority\\nof our developers are using Eclipse 3.0, some use WSAD (based on 2.1, \\nwhich does not support all the 3.0 format options), others\\nuse other IDE, Emacs etc.  If the formatter could be invoked via the\\ncommand line, then we could have consistent formatting across users, which\\nwill result in fewer diffs in our CVS commits.\\n\\nAn important part of a command line formatter would be command line options\\nto refer to a saved set of format parameters/options.\\n\\nAlthough other command line tools exist (jalopy, etc.) the Eclipse formatter\\nis the most convenient for the widest set of our internal users, so rather\\nthan force Eclipse users to replace the Eclipse formatter with an outside tool,\\nexposing the Eclipse formatter to other users is our preference.  \\n\\nA separate feature request addresses invoking the formatter via an API\\n( 46398 ) as well as 12144 to reformat multiple files in a project,\\nbut I suspect those only work within an active Eclipse session.

Summary: Batch compiler should report compilation errors to console
Description: The batch compiler used by the JDT Ant compiler adapter has a special option \\nto log compile errors to a log file if the \\"verbose\\" option is used. The \\ncurrent implementation stops logging to the error PrintWriter defined in the \\nconstructor of the batch compiler \\n(org.eclipse.jdt.internal.compiler.batch.Main) as soon as a log file is \\nspecified (verbose option is used).\\n\\nThe disadvantage is that compile warnings and errors are logged only to the \\nfile and not to the Ant console. If a logger is attached to the Ant console it \\nwill never recognize compilation errors.\\n\\nExample: The CruiseControl build system logs Ant builds to XML files (using \\nAnt XML logger). After this the XML file is used to detect failed builds \\n(builds containing compile errors) and it is transformed vie XSL into nice \\nHTML pages. This doesn't work with the JDT compiler adapter reporting compile \\nerrors to a log file.\\n\\nThe easiest solution would be to replace the error PrintWriter specified in \\nthe constructor with a \\"combined\\" PrintWriter that writes to the console and \\nto the log file.

Summary: Eclipse Java Compiler accepts string constants with UTF-8 representation larger 64kByte
Description: Dear Bugteam!\\n\\nThe Eclipse Java Compiler (Eclipse 3.0.2) accepts string constants which UTF-8 representation exceeds 64kB.\\n\\nSince Sun's Class File specification (see  http://java.sun.com/docs/books/vmspec/html/ClassFile.doc.html) defines a CONSTANT_Utf8_info structure with a length attribute of 2 byte unsigned, string constants with utf8-representation larger 65535 Bytes should not be possible.\\n\\nSuns Java Compiler (JDK 1.4.2_07 in my case) causes a compilation error, Eclipse compiler does not. \\n\\nAlthough the Eclipse compiled java class seems as if it works correctly, it is unclear if this behaviour is always correct.\\n\\nHow to reproduce: Simply define a main class and assign a very large string constant (> 64kb) to a string object.\\n\\nregards\\nMartin Purkert\\[REDACTED_EMAIL]

Summary: Tomcat 5.5.x jsp compiler emitting bad sourcefile attribute
Description: I originally posted this at apache, but they forwarded me here.\\n\\ndoing javap on a jsp generated servlet from 5.5.x starts with:\\n\\nCompiled from \\"org.apache.jsp.WEB_002dINF.jsp.components.globalheader_jsp\\"\\npublic final class org.apache.jsp.WEB_002dINF.jsp.components.globalheader_jsp \\nextends org.apache.jasper.runtime.HttpJspBase implements \\norg.apache.jasper.runtime.JspSourceDependent\\n  SourceFile: \\"org.apache.jsp.WEB_002dINF.jsp.components.globalheader_jsp\\"\\n\\nThat is, the SourceFile attribute of this class is \\n\\"org.apache.jsp.WEB_002dINF.jsp.components.globalheader_jsp\\"\\n\\nBut this is incorrect, according to the java class file specification, \\nspecifically section: 4.7.7 The SourceFile Attribute\\n\\n\\"The string referenced by the sourcefile_index item will be interpreted as \\nindicating the name of the source file from which this class file was \\ncompiled. It will not be interpreted as indicating the name of a directory \\ncontaining the file or an absolute path name for the file; such platform-\\nspecific additional information must be supplied by the runtime interpreter or \\ndevelopment tool at the time the file name is actually used.\\"\\n\\nThat means that for the above class, the SourceFile attribute should just be\\n\\n\\"globalheader_jsp.java\\"\\n\\nNote, no package or path info, as well as the .java extension.\\n\\nThis wreaks havoc on tools such as BCEL, FindBugs, etc.\\n\\noriginal tomcat bug: http://issues.apache.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=38776

Summary: "name is too long to represent" error when using JDT compiler in Tomcat for very large JSPs

Using javac the same failure does not occur. The length of the JSP and resulting source file are a key factor, which makes sense considering the JVM bug is related to lengthy debug info in the class file.\\n\\nSun may very well get around to fixing their specification issue, but JDT should work equally well as javac in the mean time.\\n\\nA second suggestion would be to have a flag that would suppress (maybe by default?) the \\"SourceDebugExtension\\" attribute as it seems unlikely the Tomcat would require this for JSP compilation.

I always use binding resolution, so I don't know if \\nthe problem shows up without.\\n\\nThe fact is that after loading all the abstract syntax trees and unloading \\nthem, even with intensive garbage collection not all memory is freed. I \\ntried on some systems, JHotDraw and jEdit, and a small amount of memory is \\nretained in all cases. I've found a quick and dirty fix for this, which is \\nto close and reopen the project which was loaded; after that, with some \\ngc'ing you get the memory back.\\n\\nTo show you this, I've built a small plug-in (see attachment) adding some menu items to Java projects in the Package explorer. One of these loads ASTs from all compilation units in the project using separate createAST calls; another one loops over finalization and garbage collection as long as the loop actually frees up something (at least 1MB). Try to use createASTs on some project (it will do garbage collection at the end), and see how much memory you recover; then close the project, and after another gc run (almost) all memory should be freed.

Summary: [1.5][compiler] Should provide option to flag unused @SuppressWarnings
ICompilationUnit.getAllTypes() throws a java.io.CharConversionException
Description: Daniel,\\n\\nI saw your name on https://www.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=108668 and wondered if you might be able to help me resolve two problems I'm having.\\n\\n1)  On Windows, a user changes the text file encoding of a Java project from the default, Cp1252 to UTF-8.  Then they invoke my action which uses JDT API to iterate IResources, IPackageFragements and ICompilationUnits and for each ICompilationUnit unit; unit.getAllTypes().  This tries to read the input stream which throws a sun.io.MalformedInputException.  Is it my responsibility as a JDT client to handle this kind of exception and tell the user the \\"text file encoding\\" may be incorrect?\\n\\nDM> You must handle the JavaModelException and present it to the user. Such a JavaModelException can wrap the encoding exception. If the ICompilationUnit.getAllTypes() throws a java.io.CharConversionException at you (which is the type to use at the Java API level) then please file a bug report against JDT Core and add myself to the CC-list.\\n\\nNOTE: Changing the encoding of a project after the files have been put in is a bad idea in general because this only specifies the encoding to be used when reading and when creating the file.\\n\\n This seems like something I as a client of JDT should not have to worry about, but currently the exception is unhandled by me and getting logged.\\n\\nDM> Verify that it is unhandled i.e. check that your code isn't getting a JavaModelException that it eventually swallows somewhere (empty catch block). If you don't get the JavaModelException then file the bug as suggested above.\\n\\n----\\n\\nDaniel, you're correct.  I was handling the JavaModelException and logging it, which is why I saw it to begin with, and it does wrap a sun.io.MalformedInputException which extends java.io.CharConversionException.  It seems this is a JDT bug.

Summary: Classes should have the same actions as CU's wherever possible
Description: I am opening this PR because an older PR containing this problem was just \\nmarked resolved/worksforme, which is not entirely accurate. The older PR is: \\nhttp://bugs.eclipse.org/bugs/show_bug.cgi?id=3750\\nIt is ok to close the older PR because the menu ordering problem has been \\ncorrected, but the \\"missing menu items\\" problem is still very much there.\\n\\nAs of 20020214-Stable build:\\n\\nGo To -> Type... is missing from the Hierarchy view\\nOpen With -> is missing from Class in Packages view\\nCopy Names is missing from the Hierarchy view\\nCut is missing from CU in Packages view\\nMove is missing from Type in Packages and in Hierarchy view\\n	(should be able to move the type or the whole CU)\\nRun/Debug is missing from the Hierarchy view\\nBut the most important missing thing from any Type is *all* of the TEAM \\nfunctions, including the whole Team -> menu, and team items in the Compare \\nWith -> menu, and Replace With -> menu.\\n\\nI will paste a bitmap of 3 menus side-by-side so that you can easily see where \\nthe gaps are. In this diagram, the menu on the left is the CU menu in the \\nPackages view, the menu in the middle is the Type menu in the Packages view, \\nand the menu on the right is the Type menu in the Hierarchy view. Ideally, all \\nmenus on Types and CUs in all perspectives should be analyzed in this visual \\nmanner - I have not used the new VAJ perspective much yet (waiting for the \\ntypes to be displayed in a hierarchy) so I did not analyze those menus, but I \\nsuspect strongly that we will discover inconsistencies and gaps if we look.\\n\\nPlease, if you don't do anything else, add team support to Types. This was done \\nin VAME and it made a huge difference. There is less mental and actual context \\nswitch required. The current implementation in Eclipse reveals that there is a \\nframework behind everything, and we do not want to let this show. The user \\nshould have a seamless experience without so many context switches. The 90% \\ncase is that the CU/Type ratio is 1:1. In the other 10% case, the tools should \\nbe able to figure out what the user meant, or if it is unclear, then just ask \\nthem.

Summary: TVT1: Apostrophe shows up multiple times in Java error messages in some translations (italian)
Description: \\r\\nSummary:\\r\\n\\r\\nJava error messages that are displayed in the Task List or status line have \\r\\ndouble apostrophes in the translated versions.  This occurs because the \\r\\ntranslators have assumed that MessageFormat would be used for messages with \\r\\nsubstitution parameters, and it requires that single quotes be doubled.  If the \\r\\nquote is not doubled, then the message is truncated.  For example:\\r\\n\\r\\n    errorMessage101=This parameter \\"{0}\\" doesn''t look right.\\r\\n\\r\\nA call to:\\r\\n\\r\\n    MessageFormat.format(errorMessage101, (new String[] {\\"x\\"})\\r\\n\\r\\nwill correctly return \\"This parameter \\"x\\" doesn't look right.\\"  However, if the \\r\\napostrophe is not doubled, the above returns \\"This parameter {0} doesn\\".  This \\r\\napparently is a well-known Java bug.\\r\\n\\r\\nA few weeks back, we discovered that the translators were not consistently \\r\\nspecifying single quotes in the message files.  Based on the assumption that \\r\\nMessageFormat would be used to insert parameters, we told them to put two \\r\\nsingle quotes if there was a message parameter present, otherwise only put one \\r\\n(with Greg Adam's agreement).  This has worked for the majority of the product.\\r\\n\\r\\nThe translators worked many hours to do so, and now we find that not all code \\r\\nuses MessageFormat.  Specifically, \\r\\n\\r\\n	org.eclipse.jdt.internal.compiler.problem.DefaultProblemFactory.getLocal\\r\\nizedMessage(int, String[])\\r\\n	org.eclipse.jdt.internal.compiler.problem.ProblemFactory.getLocalizedMes\\r\\nsage(int, String[]).\\r\\n\\r\\nThese two methods implement there own formatting, and don't expect the \\r\\nformatting rules that MessageFormat does.  This wouldn't be a big problem, \\r\\nexcept that our translators don't have a good inclination for which message \\r\\nwill be displayed by what code.  So I suggest that this code be modified \\r\\nto \\"tolerate\\" the two single quotes and treat them as one.\\r\\n\\r\\nBTW, one of the translation testers tells me that during Toronto's TVT, they \\r\\nchanged their code to use a centralized formatter that would tolerate either \\r\\nformat.  Not a bad idea for the next time around.\\r\\n\\r\\nRegards, Dan\\r\\n\\r\\nPS: This problem isn't isolated to non-English languages.  I've seen a \\r\\nfew \\"doesnt\\" and \\"dont\\" in the English product (sorry, forgot to note where).\\r\\n\\r\\n-----------------------------\\r\\n\\r\\nHere is some more details from my note to Greg Adams:\\r\\n\\r\\nSubject: Re: Translation Verification Testing - potential problem with single \\r\\nquotes  \\r\\n\\r\\nGreg,\\r\\n\\r\\nPlease see my note below for details.  Basically it boils down to this: if you \\r\\nuse MessageFormat to insert parameters into messages, then all single quotes \\r\\n(apostrophes) must be doubled.  \\r\\n\\r\\nThe translators have assumed that if a message did not have substitution \\r\\nparameters (\\"{0}\\"), then single quotes are not doubled.  If a substitution \\r\\nparameter was present, they assumed that MessageFormat would be used to insert \\r\\nthe value, so single quotes are doubled.  That seems like a reasonable \\r\\nexpectation, but I understand some in WSAD have avoided using MessageFormat \\r\\naltogther to avoid this duality.  The translators need a definitive rule to \\r\\nfollow.\\r\\n\\r\\nAre their assumptions consistent with the code?  FWIW, I'll forward you a note \\r\\nthat covers the problem in more detail.\\r\\n

Summary: Text search for 'ß' gives results for 's' (1GKQ0XA)
Description:
Text search for 'ß' gives results for 's'\\n\\n\\nNOTES:\\nDM (9/28/01 5:03:03 PM)\\n StringMatcher uses toUppercase when \\"ignore case\\" is selected.\\n This leads to errors because String.toUppercase() is not the same as\\n calling toUppercase on each character and then concatenating. In this\\n particular case 'ß' is converted to 'SS' and because the length of the\\n pattern is 1 all occurrences of 's' are reported.\\n\\n Because the uppercase conversion is only needed at one place we\\n can simply convert the characters there - no need to convert the\\n patterns itself.\\n\\n Fixed > 0.202\\n\\nNE (10/2/01 10:25:18 AM)\\n I'm fixing this up in the Navigator's StringMatcher, but couldn't find a\\n case where 'ß' is converted to 'SS'.\\n If I just do \\"ß\\".toUpperCase(), it comes back as \\"ß\\".\\n I also tried a few combinations with other characters.\\n Could you give me a case where it converts to 'SS'?\\n\\nNE (10/02/01 10:27:44 AM)\\n Never mind.\\n \\"uß\\".toUpperCase() -> \\"USS\\"\\n\\nNE (10/2/01 10:35:03 AM)\\n If I'm searching for a real word containing 'ß', and I don't care about case,\\n what's the correct behaviour?\\n E.g. if I'm searching for 'Strueßel', should it match \\"strueßel\\" and \\"STRUESSEL\\" but not \\"STRUEßEL\\",\\n or should it match \\"strueßel\\" and \\"STRUEßEL\\" but not \\"STRUESSEL\\"?\\n Please forgive the silly example.\\n\\nNE (10/2/01 12:04:13 PM) DM says:\\n The correct uppercase word for \\"strueßel\\" would be \\"STRUESSEL\\". \\n A search engine however should not be that smart. \\n I would expect to find \\"strueßel\\" and \\"STRUEßEL\\" but not \\"STRUESSEL\\". \\n Kai-Uwe which is native German confirmed that.\\n\\nNE (10/2/01 12:09:04 PM)\\n This is good, because that's what String.compareToIgnoreCase does.\\n It says:\\n * Two characters c1 and c2 are considered\\n * the same, ignoring case if at least one of the following is true:\\n *
  • The two characters are the same (as compared by the \\n * == operator).\\n *
  • Applying the method {@link java.lang.Character#toUppercase(char)} \\n * to each character produces the same result.\\n *
  • Applying the method {@link java.lang.Character#toLowercase(char) \\n * to each character produces the same result.
\\n\\n Likewise for regionMatches(...) where ignoreCase==true.\\n\\n StringMatcher should be changed to use compareToIgnoreCase.

Summary: 'Search Again' should be a tool on the search view tool bar (1GKMBM3)
Description: To rerun a Search, I have to select one of the search results and pop up a context menu,\\n	and then select 'Search Again'.\\n\\n	This is a bit obscure - I believe this action is done often enough that you:\\n	a) want users to know it exists (it's a bit of a hunt to notice it).\\n	b) want them to be able to just have to left-click on a tool (instead of right-click a menu then click the menu item)\\n\\n	So I really would like it to be a tool on the Search view's tool bar.\\n\\nNOTES:\\nEG (26.09.2001 11:07:03)\\n	Not sure I follow:\\n	1) pressing the search button shows you a dialog with all previous matches.\\n		and you can select one in the window.\\n	2) activating the drop down on the right of search allows you to do this without\\n		the dialog.\\n	what am I missing?\\n\\n	CM (9/26/01 9:33:45 AM)\\n		I guess I wanted it to be as fast as possible.\\n		(I definitely do not want to bring up the dialog again)\\n		Here is the scenario:\\n		- search for something that you want to change in a bunch of classes.\\n		- work away for a while editing the classes (which removes the search text from each class)\\n		- the list now contains extra stuff in it - some of those search results should be removed\\n		- so do a \\"search again\\" (you have to pop up the menu - here is where I wanted the tool)\\n		- the list is cleaned up for you\\n\\n		OH <DUH> I had \\"autobuild\\" turned off when I entered this PR.\\n		Or maybe I was just not saving the files (sometimes I work this way - I save all at once with 'close all' when I am making global edits).\\n		With autobuild on, and saving each file after making the change, of course the search cases are removed as you save them.\\n		So the list never becomes cluttered with stuff.\\n\\n		I wonder how many people will work with autobuild off.\\n		Probably depends on what they are doing.\\n\\n		Anyhow, the above requested feature only makes sense if autobuild is off, or if the person is lazy\\n		and does not save the files right away <g>.\\n\\n		So it's not as important as I thought - but it would be important for some people.

Summary: Scrolling to the top of page when synching packages view
Description: Eclipse 200011011\\n\\n0) Turn on the preference \\"Link packages view selection to the active editor\\".\\n1) Perform a java search on something that will have at least one result.\\n2) Look at the search and pick a class in the list of results.\\n3) Go to the packages view and make sure that a) the packages view is open, \\nvisible and not stacked with the search view and b) the class selected in the \\npackages view is not the class you picked in step 2.\\n4) In the search view, click on the entry for the class you selected in step 2.\\n\\nNotice:  The editor for that class is opened. In the end I just am forced to turn \\noff \\"Link packages view selection to the active editor\\" but then I am \\nfrustrated when I want to do something such as compare with another version and \\nI have to go hunt for the class in the packages view.

Summary: Two-step compilation:  Verify current compilation unit first, if that fails, Do not continue checking for affected CU's
Description: With a large number of projects, just the time needed to CHECK if a project or \\nclass needs to be recompiled due to a change somewhere else can take a long \\ntime.  It would be nice if compilation were broken in to two steps:  \\n\\nStep One, verify the current compilation unit.  If this passes, and the user \\nhas the \\"perform build automatically\\" preference checked, then continue with \\nincremental compilation just like it works now.  If it FAILS however, then it \\nshould be user-configurable (or default behavior) NOT to perform the auto build \\nuntil the local problem is fixed -- in other words, halt the rest of the \\ncompilation until they fix the (probably small) syntax error, and then try \\nagain next time they save. \\n\\nThis is kind of like the pop-up dialog that appeared when saving in Visual Age, \\nbut no pop-up dialog is necessary. Users will just fix the local problem and \\nthen hit save again, when everything will happen the \\"normal\\" way.  \\n\\nThis will prevent a problem I have where I compile, and because of a stupid \\nmistake I end up with two time consuming saves as WSAD cycles through all 25 \\nEJBs checking to see if they are affected -- all because I misplaced a double \\nquote.  I understand that WSAD is a bit behind the curve in incremental compile \\nspeed, but it will never be no-time. \\n\\n-Andrew

Summary: 'copy' .java file defeats 'rename' JavaDoc smartness
Description: When you rename a .java file, the rename wizard provides some smarts to fix \\nJavaDoc comments, constructors, etc.\\n\\nOne of my typical patterns is to copy a .java file and then rename it (to use \\nit as the basis for a new class).  Unfortunately this doesn't work very well.  \\nThe copy operation performs an implicit rename, fixing up the constructors, \\nclass name (and other things?). Summary: Team menu contributions on types (IType)
Description: There is a usability issue in that the team operations are not reachable in \\nsome Java views, since we only show types and not Compilation Units.\\n\\nIt is desirable to allow VCM operations on types so that users can version from \\nthe type hiearchy or the type list view. We have done the same trick in \\nVAME and it worked fine.\\n\\nTo achieve this we can change the JavaContributorResourceAdapter to map top-\\nlevel types to their containing CU. This enables the Team actions on types.\\n\\nThis results in the following problems:\\n1) VCM actions appear but are still disabled. I haven't verified it, but I \\nsuspect that VCM operations don't use the JavaContributorResourceAdapter but \\nthe IResource adapter as a consequence they target the ITypes and not the \\ncompilation units. IType returns null when asked for the adapted IResource. As \\na consequence the action appears in the menu but it is disabled. One idea would \\nbe to introduce an ITeamResourceAdapter that we could implement for Java. It \\nknows that top level types are mapped to compilation units.\\n\\n2) You get duplicate menu entries for the local history action contributions. \\nOne corresponds to the Resource actions and the other to the Java aware \\n(structure aware) local history actions.\\nThis could be solved by setting \\"adaptable\\" to false for the resource compare \\nactions (org.eclipse.compare/plugin.xml).

Summary: [assist] NPE caused by '$' in type name.
Description: Completion throws an NPE when trying to complete on \\"c.\\" in class Main below:\\n\\npublic interface Cl$ss {\\n	void test(Cl$ss c);\\n}\\npublic class Main {\\n	void m(Cl$ss c) {\\n		c.\\n	}\\n}\\n\\nthe reason for this is: method test cannot be displayed.\\nthe reason for that is: SourceTypeConverter.decodeType(String,int,int,int)\\ncreates a QualifiedTypeReference with these tokens:\\n  tokens[0] = { 'C', 'l', '$', 's', 's' }\\n  tokens[1] = null \\nThe reason behind that is: decodeType recognizes '.' I assume quite a number of places would have to\\nbe changed as to find inner classes as toplevel classes with compound\\nnames ... (the JVM-view of the world).\\n\\nwild phantasie #2:\\nCould the java model actually use two different chars to encode \\n(1) dollar-as-inner-class-delimiter and (2) dollar-as-part-of-identifier??\\n\\nquick solution(?):\\nmake extractIdentifiers(..) aware of '$' as delimiter? Summary: [1.8][compiler] analyze inheritance and overriding involving one or more default methods

Summary: [1.8][compiler] synthetic access to default method generates wrong code
Description: The following code generates wrong code:\\n\\ninterface I {\\n    public void foo() default {\\n        System.out.println(\\"default\\");\\n    }\\n}\\npublic class C implements I {\\n    public static void main(String[] args) {\\n        C c = new C();\\n        c.foo();\\n    }\\n}\\n\\nAt runtime this produces:\\nException in thread \\"main\\" java.lang.NoSuchMethodError: java.lang.Object.foo()V\\n	at C.foo(C.java:1)\\n	at C.main(C.java:9)\\n\\nThe reason is in the way a synthetic method (SuperMethodAccess) for foo is generated: it is assumed that the super method must be in accessMethod.declaringClass.superclass(), which leads to trying to invoke java.lang.Object.foo(), which obviously doesn't exist.

Summary: [1.8][compiler] Inference infrastructure should evolve to meet JLS8 18.x (Part G of JSR335 spec)
Description: BETA_JAVA8:\\n\\nA number of changes are being made to type inference mechanism to\\nfix specification bugs, clarify issues, to address poly expressions\\netc.\\n\\nThese are captured in section 18 of JLS8 - part G of JSR335 specification.\\nECJ should evolve to cope with these changes.

Summary: [1.8][compiler] implement foundation for new type inference
Description: BETA_JAVA8:\\n\\nAs a foundation for the new type inference (JSR 335) I will capture the concepts from JLS8 Section 18.1:\\n- 18.1.1 Inference Variables\\n- 18.1.2 Constraint Formulas\\n- 18.1.3 Bound Sets\\n\\nIt remains to be seen if a direct mapping of these concepts onto code yields a practical implementation:\\nPro: structural similarity will facilitate implementation and maintenance of advanced algorithms\\nCon: the new structures might conflict with our existing implementation or with performance goals.\\nLet's see.

Summary: [1.8][null] Null analysis support for lambda methods.
Description: BETA_JAVA8:\\n\\nThis may be broken. \\n\\nLambdaExpression.resolveType is an amalgam of \\n\\nMethodScope.createMethod\\nSourceTypeBinding.resolveTypesFor\\nAbstractMethodDeclaration.resolve\\n\\nI may not have hooked up all portions needed for null inheritance/analysis\\nsince some of this code was too dependent on the method binding having an\\nassociated AbstractMethodDeclaration.\\n\\nIn particular, the call to SourceTypeBinding.createArgumentBindings is\\nnot there.\\n\\nPlease see Scope.isLambdaScope, Scope.isLambdaSubscope, scope.namedMethodScope\\net al which may help with an alternate implementation.

Summary: [1.8][compiler] implement detection of poly expressions
Description: JLS8 part D defines when an expression is considered a poly expression, which depends on\\n- the kind of expression\\n- the context\\n\\nSince resolving follows different rules depending on the presence of a poly expression, this information should be obtained as early as possible.

Summary: [1.8][compiler] 'this' reference must be allowed in default methods and local classes
Description: JSR 335 0.6.1 Part H\\n\\n\\"A this expression may appear in a default method body; its type is the type of the enclosing interface. Similarly, an anonymous or local class may be declared in a default method body, so the enclosing instance of an inner class may have an interface type. \\"\\n\\nThis is actually a NOP, because this is already correctly handled by the compiler.\\nStill corresponding tests should be added.

Summary: [1.8][compiler] abstract class method should now trump conflicting default methods
Description: JSR 335 0.6.1 has a new exception in 8.4.8.4\\n\\n\\"It is a compile-time error if a class C inherits a default method whose signature is override-equivalent with another method inherited by C, unless there exists an abstract method declared in a superclass of C and inherited by C that is override-equivalent with the two methods.\\"\\n\\nThe \\"unless\\" part is new and must be implemented.

Summary: [1.8][spec] complete definition of assignment context
Description: JSR 355 0.6.1 uses the phrase \\"assignment or invocation contexts\\" to denote\\nsituations where an expression may be a poly expression.\\n\\nThe introduction of section 5 has an informal discussion \\nwhere item 2 bullet 1 starts:\\n\\n  \\"Assignment contexts (including return statements, etc.) are supported\\" \\n\\nwhich implies that the term \\"assignment context\\" is used loosely, to include\\nmany more syntactic constructs. I cannot find a precise definition for this.\\n\\nThis needs clarification, for which I could envision two alternatives:\\n(a) give a complete positive list of syntactic contexts\\n(b) explicitly extend the notion to all expression contexts *except for*\\n    statement contexts.

Summary: [1.8][compiler] don't treat default methods as overriding an independent inherited abstract method
Description: Consider this example:\\n\\npublic interface I1 {\\n	default void m() { }\\n}\\npublic abstract class C1 {\\n	public abstract void m();\\n}\\npublic class C2 extends C1 implements I1 { }\\n\\nI read the spec 0.6.1 part H, 8.4.8 as saying:\\n- I1.m is inherited because C1.m does not override it from C1\\n- C1.m is inherited because I1.m does not override it from I1\\n\\nIn 8.4.8.4 none of the sentences starting with \\"It is a compile-time error\\" apply.\\n\\nThis puts the following sentence to action:\\n\\"Otherwise, the set of override-equivalent methods consists of at least one abstract method and zero or more default methods; then the class is necessarily an abstract class and is considered to inherit all the methods.\\"\\n\\nThus we should issue an error because C2 is not abstract. This error is not reported currently.

Summary: [1.8][compiler] Compiler fails to type poly allocation expressions in method invocation contexts
In certain situations, class lookup fails for classes with dollar sign in their name
Description: I and others have observed a problem with the way Eclipse resolves classes that have a dollar sign in their name. I get errors such as \\"ASTNode$State\\" although the class clearly exists. The code compiles just fine with javac.\\n\\nWe encounter such class names in auto-generated code. The bug does _not_ seem to manifest with Eclipse versions predating the 4.x stream.\\n\\nUnfortunately, this problem occurs in a larger project in which we have a rather large set of generated classes. I tried to cut down the problem size to create a smaller error report for you but that appears to be quite hard, as often this causes the incorrect error message to mystically disappear. With the full project, the error is completely reproducible, though.\\n\\nI am therefore attaching a screenshot and the complete project as a ZIP file. I hope that will help with debugging. To reproduce the problem, just import the project into Eclipse.

Summary: [1.8][compiler] null analysis for reference expressions
Description: Bug 401030 comment 9 raised a question regarding null annotations on reference expressions.\\n\\nThis bug to address any interaction between null analysis (w/ or w/o annotations) and reference expressions.\\n\\nOne thing clearly calls for action:\\n\\n  X x = null;\\n  I i = x::bar;\\n  \\nThis should report a null reference against x but doesn't.\\n\\n\\nAs for null annotations on reference expressions it takes more investigation to see how and why this could be useful.\\n\\nThe easiest solution would be to let the target functional type completely determine any null contracts, and use only inference to see if the reference expressions meets the required null contract.\\nI'll need to play with this a bit more to see if explicit null annotations on a reference expression will be needed in some cases.

Summary: [1.8][null] TypeReference#captureTypeAnnotations treats type annotations as type argument annotations
Description: As a result, when null analysis is enabled, the following code has one compilation error where there is none when not enabled:\\n\\nimport java.lang.annotation.ElementType;\\nimport java.lang.annotation.Target;\\n\\npublic class Test {}\\n\\nclass X {\\n	class Y {\\n		public void foo( @A X. @B Y this) {}\\n	}\\n}\\n@Target(value={ElementType.TYPE_USE})\\n@interface A {}\\n@Target(value={ElementType.TYPE_USE})\\n@interface B {}\\n\\nThe result is a ParameterizedTypeBinding when null analysis is enabled and MemberTypeBinding otherwise for the explicit receiver type.

Summary: [1.8][compiler] support two phase type inference
Description: Section 18.5 distinguishes Invocation Applicability Inference (18.5.1) from Invocation Type Inference (18.5.2).\\n\\nHere the second phase is to reuse the bound set of the first phase, but any results of resolution, notably any instantiations have to be dropped and re-computed with more constraints in the lot.

Summary: [1.8][compiler] Suspect error about duplicate default methods
Description: As part of the work for upgrading our test infrastructure to use 8b81,\\nI had to modify org.eclipse.jdt.core.tests.compiler.regression.InterfaceMethodsTest.testSuperCall2\\nto be:\\n\\n// ---\\nimport java.util.*;\\nimport java.util.stream.Stream;\\npublic abstract class X<E> implements OrderedSet<E> {\\n	@Override\\n	public Stream<E> stream() {\\n		return List.super.stream(); // List is not a direct super interface\\n	}\\n	@Override\\n	public Stream<E> parallelStream() { return OrderedSet.super.parallelStream();}\\n   class Inner {\\n		public Stream<E> stream() {\\n			return OrderedSet.super.stream(); // not a super interface of the direct enclosing class\\n		}\\n	}\\n	@Override\\n	public boolean add(E o) {\\n		OrderedSet.super.add(o); // target not a default method\\n	}\\n	X() {\\n		OrderedSet.super(); // not applicable for super ctor call\\n	}\\n}\\ninterface OrderedSet<E> extends List<E>, Set<E> {\\n	@Override\\n	boolean add(E o);\\n	@Override\\n   default Spliterator<E> spliterator() { return List.super.spliterator(); }\\n}\\n// --\\n\\nThis program generates 4 errors when compiled with javac 8b81.\\nEclipse reports the same 4 errors, but in addition also reports againt\\nclass X an error about there being unrelated default methods spliterator().\\n\\nThis is suspect since OrderedSet's implementation has replaced List and Set's\\nversions and these should be out of reckoning altogether.\\n\\nSee that there is no error reported against OrderedSet itself regarding\\nduplicate unrelated defaults.\\n\\nStrangely, the unmodified method must have had the same issue - but we never\\nreported an error earlier.

Summary: [1.8][compiler] when Invocation Type Inference fails fall back to the provisional result for error reporting
Description: See, e.g., GenericTypeTest.test0805():\\n  String s = foo(numbers, floats);\\n  \\nDuring Invocation Applicability Inference we find that T = Number[], but during Invocation Type Inference we find no solution matching the expected type String.\\nThis leads the initial implementation to report: \\n  \\"The method foo(T, T) in the type X is not applicable for the arguments (Number[], Float[])\\"\\nwhere we expect:\\n  \\"Type mismatch: cannot convert from Number[] to String\\"\\n  \\nThis can be rectified by falling back to the provisional result. I have a small correction in this regard, which will later need careful integration with overload resolution.

Summary: [1.8][compiler] detect illegal reference to indirect or redundant super

Summary: [compiler][null] Bogus null warnings/errors inside unreachable code

Summary: [1.8][null] differentiate type incompatibilities due to null annotations
Description: With type annotations for null analysis, more patterns of incompatibility arise\\nwhich deserve specific analysis and reporting.\\n\\nConsider:\\n  List<@NonNull String> nonNullStrings;\\n  List<@NonNull String> nullableStrings;\\n  List<String> strings;\\n\\n(A) Incompatible:\\n  nonNullStrings = nullableStrings;\\n  nullableStrings = nonNullStrings;\\n\\n(B) Lossy (but safe) conversions:\\n  strings = nonNullStrings;\\n  strings = nullableStrings;\\n\\n(C) Unchecked, unsafe conversions:\\n  nonNullStrings = strings;\\n  nullableStrings = strings;\\n\\n\\nCurrent status:\\n\\n(A) is mostly implemented, exception:\\n - array content, nullable to nonnull incompatibility is not reported\\nCurrently, this kind of incompatibility influences overload resolution, which\\nis wrong.\\n\\n(B) works for array details, but not for type parameters.\\n\\n(C) works for type parameters but not all situations involving array details\\n\\n\\nNote, that all checking for the above happens during resolve, no flow \\nanalysis involved.

Summary: [1.8] Fully integrate type inference with overload resolution
Description: As discussed in bug 420525 comment 6 it's tricky to find the right location where type inference should be finalized, i.e., if during inference we work on lambda copies etc., at what point should this information be accepted into the original lambda?\\n\\nThe current solution works from two sides: in PGMB.computeCompatibleMethod() right after inference, and: ASTNode.resolvePolyExpressionArguments() between two possible attempts of finding a suitable method binding. This works acceptably well for simple examples but gets more and more difficult with deep nesting of poly expressions.\\n\\nLooking at the spec this issue relates to the distinction of invocation applicability inference (18.5.1) vs. invocation type inference (18.5.2). The former can be performed many times for the same invocation, and after selecting the most specific method the latter is invoked *once*.\\n\\nThus the difficulty to find the location for finalizing resolution into poly expressions relates to the fact that we haven't yet hooked invocation type inference into the proper location.\\n\\nInitial analysis suggests that\\n- invocation applicability inference corresponds to\\n  Scope.computeCompatibleMethod(MethodBinding,TypeBinding[],InvocationSite)\\n- invocation type inference corresponds to\\n  Scope.mostSpecificMethodBinding(..)\\n\\nBoth methods end up calling PGMG.computeCompatibleMethod(). Out of 8 clients calling the former, only 5 clients also call the latter.\\n\\nFor now I will draft a solution whereby these clients pass a parameter which control whether we should perform part 1 or part 2 of the inference or both.\\n\\nA final solution should later check how much of methods like mostSpecificMethodBinding should actually be *replaced* with a 1.8-specific implementation.

Description: Created attachment 250677\\nEclipse editor screenshot\\n\\nIt is possible to use JSR 305 (http://search.maven.org/#artifactdetails|com.google.code.findbugs|jsr305|3.0.0|jar) annotaions for null analysis in Eclipse.\\n\\nNamely, the following annotations can be used in place of Eclipse's standard ones (http://stackoverflow.com/questions/21375867):\\n\\n * javax.annotation.Nullable\\n * javax.annotation.Nonnull\\n * javax.annotation.ParametersAreNonnullByDefault\\n\\nIf I configure ECJ to warn on missing nullness annotation on a package, however (\\"Missing '@NonNullByDefault' annotation on package\\" -> Warning), this only works for language levels 1.7 and below.\\n\\nIf I set language level and execution environment to 1.8, the following (correct) package-info.java:\\n\\n---------------------------------------\\n@ParametersAreNonnullByDefault\\npackage com.example;\\n\\nimport javax.annotation.ParametersAreNonnullByDefault;\\n---------------------------------------\\n\\n - results in a warning:\\n\\n\\"A default nullness annotation has not been specified for the package com.example\\"\\n\\nThis is not the case with Eclipse's standard org.eclipse.jdt.annotation.NonNullByDefault annotation.

Summary: [quick fix] quick fix offers reduced set of options if cursor is not placed at the right spot
Description: Some quick fix options are only available when the cursor is placed at the right position, not when it is placed elsewhere. Consider the following example:\\n\\n------------------------------------------------\\npublic class X {\\n\\n    public X(int i) {\\n        //           ^\\n        // ----------| Put cursor here and click Ctrl+1\\n    }\\n}\\n------------------------------------------------\\n\\nThe issue (warning) here is that the constructor argument is not used. Eclipse 4.5 M5 cleverly moves the cursor to the \\"int i\\" declaration and then offers:\\n\\n- Remove 'i', keep assignments with side effects\\n- Document parameter to avoid 'unused' warning\\n- Add @SuppressWarnings 'unused' to 'i'\\n- Add @SuppressWarnings 'unused' to 'X()'\\n\\nHowever, I'm looking for another option. The option I'm looking for is only available when I click Ctrl+1 on the actual \\"int i\\" declaration, or on the light bulb at the left side of the editor:\\n\\n------------------------------------------------\\npublic class X {\\n\\n    public X(int i) {\\n        //       ^\\n        // ------| Put cursor here and click Ctrl+1\\n    }\\n}\\n------------------------------------------------\\n\\nI now get:\\n\\n- Remove 'i', keep assignments with side effects\\n- Assign parameter to new field (new, this is what I'm looking for)\\n- Document parameter to avoid 'unused' warning\\n- Rename in file (new)\\n- Rename in workspace (new)\\n- Add @SuppressWarnings 'unused' to 'i'\\n- Add @SuppressWarnings 'unused' to 'X()'\\n\\nMy suggestion is that the list of quick fixes should always be the same, regardless where I put the cursor, in this case (I love the fact that I don't have to be precise about putting the cursor on a line with a warning, btw!)

Summary: Compiler wrongly does NOT report ambiguous method call
Description: Created attachment 251341\\nSmall java program demonstrating compile problem\\n\\nBackground: we had a build failure where Maven (using the jdk1.8u40) identified a compile error due to an ambiguous method call.  The same code state compiled (and even executed successfully) in Eclipse.  \\n\\nWe confirmed that the maven executable was using the expected version of the compiler, so it boiled down to a difference between it and the Eclipse compiler.  We then convinced ourselves that the compile error was correct -- the method call was indeed ambiguous.\\n\\nTo reproduce:\\nHave a class A with method with a generic return type.  Have it return null, Object, whatever.\\nHave a class B with an overloaded method, each version accepting one parameter -- say File and String.\\nInvoke B.method(A.method)\\n\\nExpected behavior would be a compile error.  Instead, this compiles in Eclipse.  I created and attached a simple program to help reproduce the problem.\\n\\nBuild dates etc\\nWe observed the bug in Luna 4.4.1 build 20140925-1800.  I upgraded to 4.4.2 build 20150219-0600, problem still occurs.  I have a suspicion that this problem didn't exist in Keplar -- we have observed that Luna/Java 8 requires less casting.\\n\\n\\nRegarding the example file: when executed, the compiler has chosen one of the three methods over the other two.  It seems to always choose the first of the three.\\n\\nFor context, the method call in question was in a test case using Mockito, along the lines of:\\n\\n   verify(mock).overloadedMethod(anyObject(), eq(...));\\n\\nSo this problem is actually happening in the wild.

Summary: Java 8 generic method return type with wildcard in place of recursive type parameter cannot be assigned to variable with exact same type declaration
Description: Attempting to upgrade a project to Java 8 caused the Eclipse compiler and editor to freeze up on a fairly innocuous line of code.  Since I can't submit the source for the whole project, I'm creating a simple test case that replicates the pattern.  The following code shows the pattern that I believe caused the lockup, but does not actually demonstrate the lockup.  But this class compiles fine with javac and Eclipse with the Java 7 compiler, but not with Eclipse using Java 8.  The error is:\\n\\nType mismatch: cannot convert from Java8TestTrailingParams.Parameterized<?,Java8TestTrailingParams.Interface,?> to Java8TestTrailingParams.Parameterized<?,Java8TestTrailingParams.Interface,?>\\n\\nHere is the sample code:\\n\\npublic class Java8TestTrailingParams\\n{\\n    public static interface Interface\\n    {\\n    }\\n\\n    public static class Parameterized<SELF extends Parameterized<SELF, T, U>, T extends Interface, U>\\n    {\\n        @SuppressWarnings(\\"unchecked\\")\\n        SELF self() {\\n            return (SELF) this;\\n        }\\n\\n        T getEntity() {\\n            return null;\\n        }\\n    }\\n\\n    protected <T extends Interface> Parameterized<?,T,?> getParameterized(T entity)\\n    {\\n        return null;\\n    }\\n\\n\\n    public void otherMethod()\\n    {\\n        Interface entity = null;\\n        Parameterized<?, Interface, ?> parameterized = getParameterized(entity);\\n        parameterized.getEntity();\\n    }\\n}\\n\\nIf you remove the unused type parameter U from the class Parameterized, the code does compile properly using a single wild-card.  It appears that the addition of the second wild-card always causes this code to fail.\\n\\nI confess to still be occasionally befuddled by the rules around wildcards, but IMHO there absolutely must be a way in the language to specify \\"I don't care because I'm not using this type parameter anywhere\\".  Java 7 helped eliminate the clutter of redundant type declarations, and adding a cast here would be a step backwards.\\n\\nThis was tested with Eclipse Luna SR2 with the latest updates as of March 7, 2015.

Summary: [compiler][resource] potential "resource leak" problem disappears when local variable inlined
Description: I20150324-0800\\n(Found through the fix for bug 463252.)\\n\\nWhen resource leak problems are enabled in a 1.7 project, I get a potential problem on the first \\"zipFile\\" variable, and a definite problem on the second \\"zipFile\\" variable here (good):\\n\\n/**\\n * Inline zipFile => potential resource leak disappears.\\n */\\npublic class Try17 {\\n    void potential() throws IOException {\\n        ZipFile zipFile= getZipFile();\\n        String name= zipFile.getName();\\n        System.out.println(name);\\n    }\\n    void definite() throws IOException {\\n        ZipFile zipFile= new ZipFile(\\"bla.jar\\");\\n        String name= zipFile.getName();\\n        System.out.println(name);\\n    }\\n\\n    ZipFile getZipFile() throws IOException {\\n        return new ZipFile(\\"bla.jar\\");\\n    }\\n}\\n\\nWhen I inline \\"zipFile\\", the definite resource leak stays, but the potential leak disappears. I don't see why the absence of a local variable should make a difference for a potential leak.\\n\\nThe Javadocs of JavaCore.COMPILER_PB_UNCLOSED_CLOSEABLE and COMPILER_PB_POTENTIALLY_UNCLOSED_CLOSEABLE also don't reveal why that would be intended. Both only talk about a \\"local variable\\", although the definite problem also appears on an expression.

Summary: [1.8][compile] Missing semicolon in lambda body causes whole lambda expression to fail
Description: Consider the following program:\\n\\n------------------------------------------------\\npublic class T {\\n    public static void main(String[] args) {\\n        new Thread(() -> {\\n            System.out.println()\\n        });\\n    }\\n}\\n------------------------------------------------\\n\\nAll that is missing is a semi colon after the println() statement. This gets worse when the lambda body gets bigger, e.g.:\\n\\n------------------------------------------------\\npublic class T {\\n    public static void main(String[] args) {\\n        new Thread(() -> {\\n            System.out.println();\\n            System.out.println();\\n            System.out.println();\\n            System.out.println()\\n            System.out.println();\\n            System.out.println();\\n            System.out.println();\\n        });\\n    }\\n}\\n------------------------------------------------\\n\\nConversely, when using an anonymous class, the error message is precise:\\n\\n------------------------------------------------\\nSyntax error, insert \\";\\" to complete Statement\\n------------------------------------------------

Summary: ExternalAnnotationsAttachmentDialog should not allow virtual folders
Description: In bug 462768 I noticed that a virtual folder is not a good match for annotationpath, because internally we need a resolved file system path, in order to work with java.io.File. Since a virtual folder answers null to getLocation(), we should report an error when a user tries to configure a virtual folder as an annotationpath. This doesn't affected non-virtual *linked* resources, though.

Summary: Enum constants not treated as NonNull in a very specific case
Description: Minimum example:\\n\\n// File A.java:\\n\\ninterface A {\\n    enum E implements A {\\n        I;\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n\\n// File B.java\\n\\ninterface B {\\n    static int method(BinaryOperator<@NonNull A> o) {\\n        return 1;\\n    }\\n\\n    static final int X = method((a, b) -> E.I);\\n}\\n\\nThe final lines of code shows: Null type safety (type annotations): The expression of type 'A.E' needs unchecked conversion to conform to '@NonNull A'.\\n\\nCannot reproduce if the contents of B is in file A, or if you assign the lambda directly to a variable, or (most ridiculously) if `I` is statically imported (does not work if imported by wildcard).

Summary: [9] figure out glitches in spec of module-info
Description: Rereading http://cr.openjdk.java.net/~mr/jigsaw/spec/lang-vm.html (unspecified version, retrieved as of now) I'm puzzled what we should make of these:\\n\\n\\n(1): A compilation unit holding a module declaration may also contain import declarations. No text in the \\"spec\\" refers to those imports, so they appear to be without meaning.\\n\\n\\n(2) module-info.java is a compilation unit, which is member of an unnamed package. This fact doesn't seem to bear any semantics. See also 7.3, which applies to every module-info.java by construction:\\n  \\"A compilation unit that has no package declaration is part of an unnamed package (§7.4.2).\\"\\n\\n\\n(3) \\"A compilation unit (JLS 7.3) may contain a module declaration, in which case the filename of the compilation unit is typically module-info.java.\\"\\nNote the use of *typically*!! How should module declarations be handled that appear in files having a different name? Is any name legal? How are compilers supposed to find necessary module declarations?

It actually compiles to valid code due to type erasure, but javac still rejects it.\\n\\nThe example is a single file, Main.java:\\n\\n\\npackage example;\\n\\nimport java.util.Arrays;\\n\\nimport example.Ext.B;\\nimport example.Ext.C;\\n\\npublic class Main {\\n	public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {\\n		Arrays.asList(new B(), new C()); // <-- problem line\\n	}\\n}\\n\\nclass Ext {\\n	public static interface I {}\\n	private static class A {}\\n	public static class B extends A implements I {}\\n	public static class C extends A implements I {}\\n}\\n\\n----------------------------------------\\n\\njavac (jdk1.8.0_152) prints the following error:\\n\\nMain.java:10: error: incompatible types: formal varargs element type INT#1 is not accessible from class Main\\n                Arrays.asList(new B(), new C()); // <-- problem line\\n                             ^\\n  where INT#1 is an intersection type:\\n    INT#1 extends A,I\\n\\n----------------------------------------\\n\\nThe shared interface is necessary to trigger the bug in Eclipse, although hovering over asList claims that the type is inferred as \\"? extends A\\" with no mention of the interface. Summary: Consuming a binary type with MissingTypes attribute, may break existing binary type, can cause "info cannot be null"
Description: Occurred during my own development :) :\\n\\nSeeing a MissingTypes attribute while the referenced type actually exists during this compilation can cause havoc downstream, since we can't decide if this is a problem or not.\\n\\nHere's a deadly chain of events in that situation:\\n\\n- during BinaryTypeBinding.cachePartsFrom \\n  - we have a ClassFileReader with missingTypeNames containig \\"m/Issing\\"\\n  - while creating a method with the missing type in its signature\\n    we create an UnresolvedReferenceBinding with tagBits |= HasMissingType\\n\\n- from sources we reference a method from another binary type, which returns\\n  List<m.Issing>\\n  - Summary: [9][build path] Polish the new UI for modularity details
Description: As of bug 546352 class ModuleDependenciesPage has a non-blocking TODO list, to be addresses as far as possible within the 4.12 M3 time frame.\\n\\nAdditional items carried over from bug 546352:\\n\\n== Art work (icons) is not final. ==\\n\\nI have draft SVG versions for all new icons, but I wouldn't consider them 'professional' ;p (except maybe the patch icon, which I simply stole / extract from PDE). \\nAlso, the final decision regarding the patch icon has not been made:\\n\\n(In reply to Noopur Gupta from bug 546352 comment #15)\\n> - It will be good if can get some help in icon designing. If not, the\\n> current icons are fine with little changes. I think the letters 'S', 'R'\\n> etc. on the module icon can be moved closer to the 'M' icon. Currently, they\\n> stick closer to the element name instead of the module icon. For example,\\n> see entries in Details pane.\\n> \\n\\n(In reply to Stephan Herrmann from bug 546352 comment #16)\\n> (In reply to Noopur Gupta from bug 546352 comment #15)\\n> > - Not sure how the patch icon looks to everyone. Probably, a 'P' will be\\n> > more consistent.\\n> \\n> I believe a visual distinction from the other elements is good, because\\n> patching  pulls in more source folders into an existing module (thus\\n> affecting their compilation), whereas the other options only modify the API\\n> / wiring of a module.\\n> \\n> If you prefer consistency of child nodes, then I'd revive my proposal to\\n> create a new (third) toplevel node (\\"Patched with\\") - using module+patch as\\n> its icon :)\\n\\n== Revisit patch-module for options & validations ==\\n\\nWe need to validate, that no two source folders contributing to the same output folder are associated with different modules (incl. patching). See also the discussion around bug 546352 comment 23, bug 546352 comment 29, bug 546352 comment 30, bug 546352 comment 36 (should we also support binary IPackageFragmentRoot as patch locations?).\\n\\n== Additional coolness relating to CLI & m2e ==\\n\\n(In reply to Till Brychcy from bug 546352 comment #25)\\n> It would be cool if there was a button that shows the javac command line\\n> options corresponding to the combined configured details.\\n> \\n> It would be even cooler if there was another button that sets the configured\\n> details from javac command line options in the clipboard.\\n\\n(In reply to Till Brychcy from bug 546352 comment #26)\\n> Related: I just thought that m2e will want to set the configured details\\n> from command line options configured in the pom.xml, which would be a very\\n> similar functionality, so some jdt.core-api that helps with this would\\n> probably be a good idea.\\n\\n== Finalize enablement of \\"Remove\\" & provide guidance ==\\n\\n(In reply to Stephan Herrmann from bug 546352 comment #27)\\n> == bug 546352 comment 20 (b) ==\\n> \\n> > Also, the \\"Remove\\" button is enabled for the current module and for\\n> > java.base, even tough you are not allowed to remove them.\\n> \\n> Also done by intention, with the following rationale: think specifically of\\n> a multi-selection in the module list. User finds \\"Remove\\" disabled, but\\n> asks: why can't I remove those? If we keep the button enabled we have a\\n> chance to tell the reason, like: \\"Cannot remove module 'java.base'\\". User\\n> may answer: \\"oh, I didn't mean to remove java.base, thanks\\". Full list of\\n> explanations currently given this way:\\n> - \\"Cannot remove the current module\\"\\n> - \\"Cannot remove module 'java.base'\\"\\n> - \\"Cannot remove module 'foo.bar'\\n>   Only system modules can be removed here.\\n>   To remove other modules please remove them from the ModulePath (tab\\n> Projects or Libraries).\\"\\n> In particular the last scenario calls for some user guidance beyond just\\n> disabling a button, IMHO.\\n> \\n> What do others prefer?\\n> - Aggressively disable the button?\\n> - Let the user try, and tell when & why not possible?\\n> - Disable only on single selection, if illegal to remove?\\n> \\n> If you vote for disable, please suggest how the user can be guided to other\\n> tabs for removal of dependencies.\\n\\n\\n(In reply to Till Brychcy from bug 546352 comment #31)\\n> My preferred: Enable it only if at least one removable item is selected (and\\n> when remove is clicked, and some non-removable ones are selected, remove the\\n> removable ones but give a message as written above for the others)\\n\\n(In reply to Till Brychcy from bug 546352 comment #32)\\n> Only later I understood that \\"remove\\" is used both for modules and for\\n> configured details. I don't have a better suggestion yet. Maybe moving the\\n> \\"Add System Modules..\\" button to the other buttons on the right would help?\\n> But I'm not convinced myself. Maybe the button title could dynamically\\n> change if removable items are selected to either \\"Remove system module\\" or\\n> \\"Remove configured detail\\" (or the corresponding plural forms).\\n> \\n> In the other comment you asked how to guide users how to remove non-system\\n> modules. Now I actually wondered if the question shouldn't be: How to guide\\n> users how to *add* non-system modules here (Removing them the same way would\\n> then be natural)\\n\\n== Linked Help ==\\n\\nTo be authored and linked into the dialog.\\n\\n--------------------------------\\nWe should also consider removing the old UI, either for M3 or in 4.13.

Summary: removing a system module should be possible even if it is (indirectly) required
Description: When a module requires a deprecated system module, users should migrate to a 3rd party library. To do so they currently have to do some extra steps:\\n\\n1. remove \\"requires\\"\\n2. remove the system module from the build path (Module Dependencies tab)\\n3. add the 3rd party library\\n4. re-add \\"requires\\"\\n\\nSteps 1 & 4 are needed because we currently refuse to remove a required module.
